details: Oil prices have reportedly fallen to levels seen before the recent Iran conflict, as more tankers are now transiting the Strait of Hormuz. This comes despite Iran's warnings against unauthorized crossings, following the U.S. Secretary of State's assertion that the U.S. will not accept the Strait belonging exclusively to any single nation. The increased vessel traffic suggests a de-escalation of immediate maritime tensions in the crucial oil chokepoint.
title: Oil Prices Fall to Pre-Iran War Levels Amid Hormuz De-escalation

details: Two powerful earthquakes, measuring 7.5 and 7.2 magnitude, have hit Venezuela, prompting the government to declare a state of emergency. The quakes have resulted in at least 164 fatalities, with rescue teams actively searching for survivors. Global leaders have expressed solidarity with Venezuela following the widespread devastation.
title: Devastating Earthquakes Strike Venezuela, State of Emergency Declared

details: The Trump administration has formally requested $87.6 billion in spending, a portion of which is designated for the ongoing conflict with Iran. President Trump also criticized NATO members for what he described as lax participation in the war. U.S. Secretary of State Rubio affirmed the U.S. is "completely aligned" with its Gulf allies on Iran policy.
title: Trump White House Requests $87.6 Billion for Iran War Amid NATO Criticism
